status: documented fault models for STEaR; not exhaustive - unmodeled causes are reported as unknown_fault

semantics.signature_any: Claims characteristic of the fault AT the hypothesis location. Any present -> signature confirmed. All observed absent -> hypothesis contradicted. Otherwise unconfirmed (plausible, needs evidence).
semantics.signature_scope: 'location' (default): signature must be observed at the location itself. 'scope': anywhere within the location's impact scope (used for services observed through their dependents).
semantics.require_absent: Claims that must be observed ABSENT at the location to confirm (present -> contradicted; missing -> unconfirmed).
semantics.contradicted_by: Claims whose presence at the location contradicts the hypothesis (missing is fine).
semantics.corroborating: Claims at the location that add support when present.
semantics.effects: Claims the fault can cause at any entity inside its impact scope (topology-derived).
semantics.location_types: Allowed topology node types for node-located faults (ignored without topology).
semantics.signature_contradiction: 'all_absent' (default): contradicted only when every signature claim is observed normal. 'any_absent': contradicted when at least one signature claim is observed normal and none is present - used when the listed claims are alternative counters of ONE physical phenomenon, so one normal reading is informative.
semantics.service_kinds: For service-located faults: allowed topology service_kind values (nodes without a declared kind are allowed, with a limitation).
semantics.contradicted_if_absent: Claims whose fresh NORMAL reading at the location contradicts the hypothesis (e.g. a device that answers reachability probes is not down). Missing is fine.
semantics.identifiability: If all findings confirming a selected cause are also predicted by a surviving competitor with missing discriminators, the outcome is ambiguous until the competitor's discriminating observation is obtained.

recommendations: Identify top talkers and traffic classes on {location} using existing flow/telemetry tools (read-only)
Review QoS policy and capacity of {location}; plan an uplink upgrade or load-balancing if utilization stays high
Correlate with scheduled jobs (backups, updates) during the incident window
Inspect cabling, transceiver/optic levels and duplex/speed negotiation on {location}
Check the peer interface counters for matching errors
Schedule a maintenance window to replace the cable or optic if errors keep increasing
INTERFACE_DEGRADATION.modeling_note: Physical-layer degradation (cable/optic/duplex) increments CRC/FCS or input-error counters; a fresh normal reading of either counter with neither elevated is treated as contradicting it.

recommendations: Check physical link state and logs on {location} and its peer
Verify whether a redundant path exists and whether traffic failed over
Inspect the process/CPU breakdown on {location} (control-plane load, logging, routing churn) using read-only commands
Check for broadcast storms or control-plane policing drops affecting {location}
caveats: High CPU co-occurring with symptoms does not by itself prove it caused them

recommendations: Check power, console access and last logs of {location}
Confirm the outage scope and whether redundant devices took over
Survey coverage around {location}; check AP transmit power and placement
Check whether clients are associating to a distant AP (sticky clients)
Run a spectrum/channel-utilization check near {location}; consider changing channel or channel width
Look for non-Wi-Fi interferers and overlapping neighbouring APs
Check the DNS service {location}: process health, upstream forwarders and recent configuration changes
Test name resolution from an affected segment against {location} and an alternate resolver (read-only)
Check the DHCP service {location}: scope exhaustion, relay (ip-helper) configuration and service health
Compare new-lease failures with existing clients' connectivity

coverage_domains._semantics: A 'healthy' verdict requires a fresh normal ('absent') finding for at least one claim of every domain the topology says exists. Missing data is not evidence of normality. Unmonitored domains make the outcome insufficient_evidence and the planner may request coverage from authorized recorded sources.
